denomProfiles/seventh-day-baptists/tagli: Baptists who keep Saturday, the seventh day, as the Sabbath.
denomProfiles/seventh-day-baptists/coreD: The seventh day (Saturday) is the biblical Sabbath to be kept holy.
Salvation by grace through faith; Sabbath-keeping as obedience, not a means of salvation.
Congregational autonomy and liberty of conscience.
denomProfiles/seventh-day-baptists/focus: Missions in Africa, Asia and Latin America through a world federation.
denomProfiles/seventh-day-baptists/pract: Worship on Saturday, the Sabbath beginning at sunset on Friday.
General Conference of North America (1802) linking churches, now based at Janesville, Wisconsin.
Seventh Day Baptist World Federation linking national conferences.
denomProfiles/seventh-day-baptists/influ: Rachel Oakes Preston, a Seventh Day Baptist, introduced the Sabbath to Adventists at Washington, New Hampshire, in 1844.
Shared Sabbatarian convictions in the nineteenth century.
denomProfiles/seventh-day-baptists/keyFi: Seventeenth-century Sabbatarian pastor in London, died in Newgate prison
Brought Sabbatarian views to Newport, Rhode Island, in 1664
Seventh Day Baptist who brought Sabbath-keeping to the Adventists
denomProfiles/free-will-baptists/tagline: Arminian Baptists: free grace for all, believers' freedom, and foot washing.
denomProfiles/free-will-baptists/coreDoc: General atonement: Christ died for all people.
Free will: grace enables every person to accept or reject salvation.
Conditional security: a believer can fall away through persistent unbelief.
The Treatise of the Faith and Practices of the National Association (1935).
denomProfiles/free-will-baptists/focuses: Evangelism and revival in the American South and Midwest.
Holy living and conservative evangelical ethics.
denomProfiles/free-will-baptists/practic: Three ordinances: baptism, the Lord's Supper and the washing of the saints' feet.
Congregational government with associations and a National Association (1935).
Pastors are men in most churches.
denomProfiles/free-will-baptists/influen: Most northern (Randall) Free Baptists merged with Northern Baptists in 1911.
Free Will Baptists in North Carolina who accepted Pentecostal teaching after 1907.
denomProfiles/free-will-baptists/keyFigu: Organised the first southern Free Will Baptist church (1727)
Founded the northern Freewill Baptist movement at New Durham, New Hampshire (1780)
denomProfiles/free-will-baptists/inIndia: The northern Freewill Baptists ran a mission at Balasore and Midnapore in Odisha and Bengal from 1836; after the 1911 merger it passed to the American Baptists.
denomProfiles/nigerian-baptist-conventio: One of the world's largest Baptist conventions, rooted in Yorubaland since 1850.
Evangelical Baptist faith: salvation by grace through faith in Christ.
Believer's baptism by immersion and the Lord's Supper.
Authority of Scripture and local church autonomy.
A confession in the Southern Baptist tradition.
Evangelism and church planting across Nigeria and in neighbouring countries.
Education: schools, the Nigerian Baptist Theological Seminary at Ogbomoso and Bowen University (Iwo, 2001).
Medical work, including the Baptist hospital at Ogbomoso.
Christian witness in a religiously plural nation, including in northern states.
Worship in Yoruba, English and many other Nigerian languages.
Associations and conferences under a national convention based at Ibadan.
Strong women's and youth organisations.
Lively music and prayer meetings alongside Baptist order.
Baptist work in West Africa
Nigerian Baptists send missionaries to neighbouring countries and beyond.
Baptist World Alliance
Among the largest member bodies of the BWA.
Thomas Jefferson Bowen
Pioneer Southern Baptist missionary in Yorubaland from 1850
Mojola Agbebi
Lagos Baptist leader of the 1888 Native Baptist church and of African church independence
denomProfiles/brazilian-baptist-conventi: Brazil's leading historic Baptist body, planted from Salvador in 1882.
Evangelical Baptist faith: salvation by grace through faith in Christ.
Believer's baptism by immersion and the Lord's Supper.
Authority of Scripture and local church autonomy.
Religious liberty and separation of church and state.
Evangelism and church planting across Brazil.
National and world missions boards sending Brazilian missionaries abroad.
Theological education, including the South Brazil Baptist Theological Seminary in Rio de Janeiro (1908).
Social and educational work.
Congregational government with state conventions and a national assembly.
Hymnody from the Cantor Cristão, the Brazilian Baptist hymnal.
Worship styles ranging from traditional to contemporary.
Lord's Supper as a memorial, often monthly.
Convenção Batista Nacional
Charismatic churches excluded in 1965 formed the National Baptist Convention.
Brazilian Baptist missions
Brazilian missionaries serve in Portuguese-speaking Africa and elsewhere.
William Buck Bagby
Southern Baptist missionary and co-founder of the first church at Salvador
Anne Luther Bagby
Missionary educator and co-founder
Zachary Clay Taylor
Missionary co-founder at Salvador
Antônio Teixeira de Albuquerque
Former Catholic priest, the first Brazilian Baptist pastor
denomProfiles/methodist/tagline: Wesley's revival: grace for all, warm-hearted faith and holy living.
denomProfiles/methodist/coreDoctrines/0: Prevenient grace: God's grace goes before every person, enabling a free response.
denomProfiles/methodist/coreDoctrines/1: Justification by faith and the witness of the Spirit (assurance).
denomProfiles/methodist/coreDoctrines/2: Christian perfection or entire sanctification: love made perfect in this life.
denomProfiles/methodist/coreDoctrines/3: Universal offer of salvation, against unconditional predestination.
denomProfiles/methodist/coreDoctrines/4: Doctrinal standards in Wesley's Sermons, Notes on the New Testament and the Articles of Religion.
denomProfiles/methodist/coreDoctrines/5: Scripture as primary, read with tradition, reason and experience (the "Wesleyan quadrilateral", Albert Outler's term).
denomProfiles/methodist/focuses/0: Evangelism and preaching to the poor, outdoors if need be.
denomProfiles/methodist/focuses/1: Social holiness: schools, hospitals, temperance and anti-slavery.
denomProfiles/methodist/focuses/2: Small-group discipleship in class meetings and bands.
denomProfiles/methodist/focuses/3: Sung theology through Charles Wesley's hymns.
denomProfiles/methodist/practices/0: A connexion of societies governed by Conference, with ministers stationed by appointment.
denomProfiles/methodist/practices/1: Infant baptism and the Lord's Supper, Wesley urging "constant communion".
denomProfiles/methodist/practices/2: Covenant service, love feasts and watchnight services.
denomProfiles/methodist/practices/4: Hymn singing at the centre of worship.
denomProfiles/methodist/influenced/0/tex: Developed Wesley's teaching on entire sanctification.
denomProfiles/methodist/influenced/2/tex: The AME and AME Zion churches arose within American Methodism.
denomProfiles/methodist/influenced/3/tex: William Booth was a Methodist New Connexion minister.
denomProfiles/methodist/keyFigures/0/rol: Founder and organiser of the Methodist movement
denomProfiles/methodist/keyFigures/3/rol: Bishop who spread Methodism across early America
denomProfiles/methodist/keyFigures/4/rol: First superintendent of American Methodism and promoter of missions
denomProfiles/methodist/members/note: World Methodist Council's published figure of about 80 million people in its member churches, including Wesleyan, holiness and united churches.
denomProfiles/methodist/inIndia: British Wesleyans worked in Madras and the Tamil country from 1817 and their churches joined the Church of South India in 1947; American Methodist Episcopal work from Bareilly (William Butler, 1856) grew into the Methodist Church in India, autonomous since 1981.
denomProfiles/holiness-movement/tagline: Nineteenth-century revival of Wesley's call to entire sanctification.
denomProfiles/holiness-movement/coreDoct: Entire sanctification as a second, instantaneous work of grace after conversion.
Heart purity and perfect love made possible by the Holy Spirit.
Phoebe Palmer's "altar theology": consecrate all and claim the promise by faith.
Salvation offered to all, received by faith.
Strict personal ethics and separation from worldliness.
denomProfiles/holiness-movement/focuses/: Holiness literature, periodicals and Bible schools.
Ministry to the urban poor and rescue missions.
Women's preaching, defended by Palmer in Promise of the Father (1859).
denomProfiles/holiness-movement/practice: National Camp Meeting Association for the Promotion of Holiness (Vineland, New Jersey, 1867).
Testimony meetings and altar calls for sanctification.
Plain dress and abstinence from alcohol and tobacco in many groups.
Simple, revivalist worship with gospel songs.
denomProfiles/holiness-movement/influenc: Parham and Seymour taught Spirit baptism as a further blessing after sanctification.
The largest denomination formed from holiness associations.
Daniel S. Warner's 1881 movement for holiness and Christian unity.
Began as a holiness body before becoming Pentecostal.
The British "higher life" movement (1875) was a Reformed counterpart.
denomProfiles/holiness-movement/keyFigur: Lay theologian, author of The Way of Holiness (1843)
Revivalist and Oberlin teacher of perfection
First president of the National Camp Meeting Association
Founder of the Church of God (Anderson)
denomProfiles/holiness-movement/inIndia: Holiness bodies including the Salvation Army, Free Methodists, Nazarenes and the Church of God (Anderson) have Indian churches; Union Biblical Seminary, founded at Yavatmal in 1938 by a Free Methodist missionary and now at Pune, has trained many Indian evangelical leaders.
denomProfiles/salvation-army/tagline: A holiness church organised as an army, joining evangelism with social service.
denomProfiles/salvation-army/coreDoctrin: Eleven articles of faith, evangelical and Wesleyan in character.
Salvation by grace through faith, offered to all.
Entire sanctification: holiness of heart and life.
Sacraments not observed outwardly since 1883; the life of grace is held to be possible without them.
The Trinity, the full deity and humanity of Christ, and the authority of Scripture.
denomProfiles/salvation-army/focuses/0: Evangelism among the poor, the homeless and the excluded.
denomProfiles/salvation-army/focuses/1: Social service: shelters, rehabilitation, disaster relief and anti-trafficking work.
denomProfiles/salvation-army/focuses/2: Total abstinence from alcohol and non-medical drugs for soldiers.
denomProfiles/salvation-army/focuses/3: Equal ministry of women and men as officers from the start.
denomProfiles/salvation-army/practices/0: Uniforms, ranks, corps (local churches) and officers (ordained ministers).
denomProfiles/salvation-army/practices/1: Soldiers enrolled by signing the Soldier's Covenant.
denomProfiles/salvation-army/practices/2: Brass bands, songsters and open-air meetings.
denomProfiles/salvation-army/practices/3: The mercy seat, where people kneel to pray for salvation or holiness.
denomProfiles/salvation-army/practices/4: An international General elected by the High Council (since 1929).
denomProfiles/salvation-army/influenced/: In Darkest England and the Way Out (1890) shaped Christian social work; the 1885 "Maiden Tribute" campaign helped raise the age of consent.
A model for rescue missions and Christian relief organisations.
denomProfiles/salvation-army/keyFigures/: Co-founder, preacher and advocate of women's ministry
Pioneer of the work in India from 1882
denomProfiles/salvation-army/inIndia: Frederick Booth-Tucker landed in Bombay in 1882 and adopted Indian dress; the Army grew strongest in Kerala and southern Tamil Nadu (Catherine Booth Hospital, Nagercoil) and ran colonial-era settlements for so-called Criminal Tribes.
denomProfiles/african-methodist-episcopa: The first independent Black denomination in the US, born of protest at segregation.
Methodist doctrine in the Articles of Religion inherited from Wesley.
Salvation by grace through faith for all, and growth in holiness.
Human equality before God: "God our Father, Christ our Redeemer, Man our Brother".
Infant and adult baptism and the Lord's Supper as sacraments.
Black self-determination and dignity in church and society.
Education: Wilberforce University (bought by the church in 1863) and other colleges.
Civil rights and community uplift.
Missions in Africa and the Caribbean.
Episcopal government with bishops, General Conference every four years and districts.
Methodist liturgy with spirited Black preaching and music.
Monthly communion in many congregations.
Publishing through the Christian Recorder (from 1852).
Women ordained; Vashti McKenzie became the first woman bishop in 2000.
Ethiopian movement in South Africa
Mangena Mokone's Ethiopian Church joined the AME in 1896.
Black church tradition
A model of independent Black church life across the US.
Back-to-Africa movements
Bishop Henry McNeal Turner promoted African emigration.
Richard Allen
Founder and first bishop (1816)
Jarena Lee
First woman authorised to preach by Allen (1819)
Daniel Alexander Payne
Bishop and educator, president of Wilberforce
Henry McNeal Turner
Bishop and advocate of African missions
Vashti Murphy McKenzie
First woman bishop (2000)
